newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Oct 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Oct 30.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Anglo American has become the largest shareholder of British conglomerate Lonrho after German financier Dieter Bock exercised his right to sell his 18.3 percent Lonrho stake to Anglo for 257 million stg.
- The Johannesburg Stock Exchange took a hammering yesterday, gilt yields pierced key levels and interest rate jitters intensified as the rand's meltdown continued.
- An extradition order was granted for one of South Africa's most wanted fugitives, Oliver Hill, after a lengthy hearing in London's Bow Street Magistrate's Court.

- Black empowerment group Real Africa Investments Ltd, long mooted to be the main contender for Anglo American's unbundling of its 47 percent interest in JCI, has decided not to puruse the deal, chairman Don Ncube said.
- Taiwan has accused South Africa of dragging its heels on a proposed $3.5 billion petrochemical complex joint-venture in the Eastern Cape.
- Calls for a quicker abolition of exchange controls, fuelled by the rand's third record low in as many trading days, are unreasonable, Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals said.
- Parliament will vote abortion-on-request legislation into law after the National Party forced a one-day delay and threatened a Constitutional Court challenge.

- Security police, acting on orders "from the top", tortured to death at least five anti-apartheid activists and eliminated a number of others in what was described before the Truth and Reconciliation Commission as a "war without rules" during the late 1980s.
